content: The excursion was as described. We were picked up on time and the schedule was adhered to. We were the only two tourists who didn't speak Mandarin, and we had a dedicated guide to translate what the main guide said into English. The first part at Shanghai Film Park was very good, although it felt rushed. What we enjoyed less was the visit to the old city. The guide only gave very quick explanations for the rest of the time. He organized the boat trip well, but for the rest of the tour, until we returned to the bus, we were on our own. We expected to learn about the history of the city and its inhabitants, but there was nothing at all. It's primarily a tourist attraction. It's very pretty, but if, like us, you were expecting a historical tour, you might be disappointed. Overall, it was a good experience, and we were happy with the tour.

content: I've brought relatives and friends to Yu Garden many times, but each time we only visited the Nine-Turn Bridge, the Green Wave Corridor, and the Lake Pavilion. Today, I discovered that the garden itself is a hidden gem. Every stone, every hill, every tree, every lion, dragon, toad, and mud brick sculpture, all unfolded before me through the flowing river of history, thanks to Teacher Mao's eloquent narration. The Jade Linglong Stone, a relic of Emperor Huizong of Song's "Flower and Stone Tribute," the iron lion still gleaming from the Yuan Dynasty, the imposing and beautiful rockery, the 400-year-old ginkgo tree, and the Dianchun Hall, which witnessed the rise and fall of the Pan Mansion, the Sugar Industry Guild, and the Small Swords Society—all speak of aesthetics and the passage of time. Thank you, Teacher Mao, for your wonderful and vivid explanation. Leaving the garden, I revisited the Nine-Turn Bridge and the Green Wave Corridor, savoring the pavilions, terraces, flowers, rocks, and plants behind them, and bought a butterfly pastry, the same kind used by British Prime Minister Starmer. I'm already thinking that next time friends visit, I'll definitely bring them to appreciate the cultural atmosphere of this place again.
